title: 进化生物学 Day 22：微生物组与共生
title_en: Evolutionary Biology Day 22: The Microbiome and Symbiosis

questions.question: 蚜虫体内的布赫纳氏菌住在宿主细胞里、吃宿主的东西，却从不「多拿一点、少给一点」。最准确的解释是什么？
options: 它只能经卵传代，多拿的变异缩小了自己唯一的出口，留不下来
蚜虫的免疫系统能识别并清除多拿养分的菌株，这种惩罚让作弊得不偿失
它的基因组已缩减到约五百八十个基因，早就没有多拿养分的能力了
长期共演化让菌群整体形成了合作倾向，作弊在群体层面上被选择淘汰
questions.explanation: 关键是传递通道：菌的拷贝只能坐在卵里出去，宿主多一个后代它就多一批拷贝，宿主死了它这条线就断，于是作弊的品系没传下来，不是它选择了忠诚。基因组缩减是长期只随卵传之后的结果，不是它不作弊的原因，把因果倒过来了。
questions.question_en: Buchnera bacteria live inside aphid cells and feed on the host, yet never evolve to take a little more and give a little less. What is the most accurate explanation?
options_en: It can only leave through the mother's eggs, so greedier strains shrink their own only exit and die out
The aphid's immune system detects and clears strains that take extra nutrients, and that punishment makes cheating a losing bet
Their genome has shrunk to about 580 genes, so they no longer have the capacity to take extra nutrients
Long coevolution has given the bacterial population a cooperative disposition, and cheating is selected out at the group level
questions.explanation_en: The key is the transmission channel. Copies of the bacterium can only leave inside an egg, so every extra host offspring means more copies and a dead host ends the line; cheating strains simply left no descendants, and nothing chose loyalty. Genome reduction is a consequence of long-term egg-only transmission, not the reason they don't cheat, so that option reverses cause and effect.

questions.question: 在一种昆虫身上发现了一种新的细菌，它和布赫纳氏菌一样只随卵传给下一代，精子里没有它。仅凭这一点，能推出什么？
options: 它与宿主的繁殖成功已经绑成同一个数，迟早会演化成像布赫纳氏菌那样的互利共生
不能断定利益一致：雄性对它是死胡同，它可能把性别比往雌性掰
它会像线粒体那样不断丢基因，最终变成宿主细胞里一个不再独立的细胞器
既然只走母系一条通道，它不可能在种群里扩散得比不带菌的个体更快
questions.explanation: 沃尔巴克氏体也只随卵传，却用杀雄、雄变雌、孤雌生殖和胞质不亲和在种群里铺开，对昆虫毫无好处。文中的结论是：出口窄不等于利益对齐，要看窄在哪儿。它只搭雌性这条线，所以与宿主整体的繁殖成功并没有绑成同一个数。
questions.question_en: A new bacterium is found in an insect. Like Buchnera, it is passed to offspring only through eggs and never through sperm. What can be concluded from that fact alone?
options_en: Its reproductive success is now locked to the host's, so it will eventually become a mutualist like Buchnera
Not that interests align: males are a dead end for it, so it may skew the host's sex ratio toward females
Like mitochondria, it will keep shedding genes until it becomes an organelle that is no longer independent of the host cell
Since it only travels down the maternal line, it can't spread through a population faster than uninfected individuals
questions.explanation_en: Wolbachia also travels only in eggs, yet it spreads through populations via male-killing, feminization, parthenogenesis and cytoplasmic incompatibility, with no benefit to the insect. The piece's point is that a narrow exit doesn't guarantee aligned interests; it depends on where the bottleneck sits. Riding only the female line, it isn't tied to the host's overall reproductive success.

questions.question: 有人主张把宿主和它身上的全部微生物当作一个「全生物」，让自然选择作用在这个整体上。按文中采用的判据，要判断某个宿主和菌的组合能不能这样当成一个演化单位，关键看什么？
options: 微生物的细胞数量是否和宿主细胞相当，甚至多于宿主细胞
这整套组成是否可靠地、成套地一起传给宿主的下一代
这些微生物对宿主生理是否不可或缺，缺了它宿主就发育异常
宿主和微生物在代谢上是否互补，彼此稳定地交换养分
questions.explanation: 能不能当成单位来结算，取决于整套是否连续地一起传下去：蚜虫和布赫纳氏菌满足，人和肠道菌群不满足，因为人的大多数肠道菌是陆续从环境中捡来的、随时会换。无菌小鼠发育异常说明菌很重要，但重要不等于成套遗传，这正是文中先承认、再说明不够的那部分。
questions.question_en: Some argue that a host and all its microbes should be treated as a single holobiont, with natural selection acting on the whole. By the criterion the piece adopts, what decides whether a given host–microbe combination can be treated as an evolutionary unit?
options_en: Whether microbial cells are as numerous as the host's own cells, or more so
Whether the whole set is reliably passed to the next generation together, as a package
Whether the microbes are physiologically essential, such that the host develops abnormally without them
Whether host and microbes are metabolically complementary, stably exchanging nutrients
questions.explanation_en: Whether something can be treated as a unit depends on whether the package is passed on together, generation after generation. Aphids and Buchnera qualify; humans and their gut flora don't, because most gut microbes are picked up piecemeal from the environment and can change at any time. Abnormal germ-free mice show that microbes matter, but mattering isn't the same as being inherited as a set. The piece grants that point and then explains why it isn't enough.
